status_detail: Searched county/EDA and web for data center/server farm/colocation items. Cecil County economic development markets industrial sites such as Principio Business Park as suitable for data center uses, but I found no named data center project, permit, rezoning, tax abatement, or local approval record in the county.
notes: County EDA page lists data center as an ideal use for Principio Business Park; treated as site marketing, not a project.

status_detail: TeraWulf announced acquisition of the Morgantown Generating Station in Charles County on February 2, 2026; company materials describe approximately 210 MW of current generation, 250 buildable acres, a path to support up to 1 GW of load, and an initial development approach of approximately 500 MW. Later local reporting says FERC approved the plant sale, but that approval did not itself approve data center construction.
notes: Capacity_mw set to initial phase described by TeraWulf; notes preserve 1 GW ultimate load pathway. County EDA has a Morgantown major-project page referencing TeraWulf's 2026 acquisition.

status_detail: Searched county site and local news. Dorchester County considered and adopted a temporary moratorium on data centers in August 2026, but I found no named data center application or project in Dorchester County, Maryland.
notes: Avoided Dorchester County, SC Google projects as wrong state. Facebook official county post indicates Resolution No. 712 moratorium; no project name found.

aliases: Quantum Frederick hyperscale data center campus
status_detail: Frederick County Office of Economic Development describes Quantum Frederick as a 2,100-acre master-planned hyperscale data center campus on the former Eastalco aluminum site, with Catellus selected as lead developer in 2024, approximately 17.4 million square feet of entitled data center space, and 2.4 GW of power. County government says current construction work is not stopped by its July 1, 2026 pause on new applications.
notes: County page explicitly distinguishes the 2026 pause on new applications from work already under construction.

status_detail: Frederick County EDA lists Aligned Data as a data center opportunity; Aligned's Maryland page identifies IAD-04 at 5601 Manor Woods Road, Frederick, MD 21703 as a 75-acre campus designed to Tier III standards. The page markets the Frederick campus for AI-ready data center capacity but does not disclose total MW.
notes: Aligned page provides campus/address details but not total capacity; no MW inferred from backup generator/UPS component bullets.

status_detail: Frederick County EDA lists Rowan Digital Infrastructure Bauxite I, II, III as a data center opportunity. Rowan's portfolio page lists Bauxite 1, 2, 3 and a 300 MW, 400-acre project with completion shown as 2027; third-party project summaries place it within the Quantum Loophole/Frederick campus.
notes: Rowan public portfolio is sparse but official; Baxtel adds project-location context and building count/square footage, so those details are kept out of structured fields.

project_name: Amazon AWS BWI / IAD534 Bauxite II
status_detail: Maryland Department of the Environment issued an air quality permit for Amazon's proposed data center facility on Digital Drive/Frederick, authorizing 99 diesel emergency backup generators. MDE public-review materials identify IAD534/Bauxite II and state Amazon is entering a lease with Rowan for the campus.
notes: MDE PDF is official for IAD534/Bauxite II; local news confirms permit issuance. DataCenterMap also lists existing AWS BWI buildings near Mountville Road/Ballenger Creek Pike.

project_name: Social Security Administration Frederick data center
status_detail: Frederick County EDA lists the Social Security Administration data center among other data centers in Frederick County and describes it as processing 75 million transactions per day. Historic coverage reported SSA bought land in Frederick County in 2011 for a 400,000-square-foot data center near Fannie Mae's existing facility.
notes: County EDA page verifies presence/operation; no public MW found in quick pass.

status_detail: Frederick County EDA lists the Fannie Mae Regional Data Center as a 220,000-square-foot facility with 90,000 square feet of office, 60,000 square feet of data center, and 70,000 square feet of MEP space. A 2026 JLL listing for Fannie Mae Tech Center at 9107 Bennett Creek Boulevard describes 4.3 MW of installed critical capacity and 5.5 MW of expansion capacity.
notes: Capacity_mw uses installed critical capacity from JLL listing; Gensler gives design/project context with a slightly different square-foot figure.

project_name: Former Verso Luke mill potential data center
status_detail: Local Garrett County reporting described residents gathering in March 2026 to discuss rumors of a potential data center at the former Verso Luke mill site. Garrett County business-development searches turned up Maryland Tech Council data-center summit/start-up items but no county application, developer announcement, permit, or approval for this site.
notes: Included for recall because brief asks broad coverage; evidence is rumor/local discussion, not a confirmed project.

project_name: Mountain Branch Golf Club AI Infrastructure Campus
status_detail: Local news reported a developer proposal for an AI Infrastructure Campus at Mountain Branch Golf Club. Harford County subsequently enacted Bill 26-011 banning data centers; the county executive's June 10, 2026 statement says data centers were not a permitted use and that the legislation was intended to prevent opening Harford County to data centers.
notes: Structured as rejected because the county-wide ban blocks the reported proposal; developer identity and capacity were not confirmed in official materials.

aliases: Microsoft Dorsey Run Road data center
Annapolis Junction Business Park data center
status_detail: A county variance package for 8201/8211/8231/8241/8251 Dorsey Run Road describes a forthcoming grading/building permit to construct a three-story data center building of approximately 171,726 square feet plus administration space, an onsite substation, and future buildings on Microsoft-owned lots. Howard County separately enacted a moratorium on new data center approvals through November 2, 2027; tracker records list this Microsoft facility in Howard County at 8201 Dorsey Run Road with an approved existing-update permit.
notes: Location is near the Howard/Anne Arundel boundary; the most detailed official permit package is from Anne Arundel County, while tracker data assigns 8201 Dorsey Run Road to Howard County. Kept because Annapolis Junction is commonly associated with Howard County and the batch is county-level recall.

status_detail: Searched Kent County, MD official/business pages and local references. Found a 2020 Kent Conservation and Preservation Alliance item about a proposed land-use ordinance that would allow data processing centers, and county demographic/data resources, but no named Kent County, Maryland data center project, application, or approval. Many current search hits refer to Kent County, Delaware or Kent County, Michigan and were excluded.
notes: No active project found; watch for false positives from Kent County, DE and MI.

developer: Terra Energy LLC / Atmosphere Data Centers
status_detail: Montgomery Planning staff report for Conditional Use CU202413 describes a request to construct and operate data centers and battery storage at the decommissioned Dickerson power plant, with three land bays and a general approval process requiring later detailed site plans for each phase. Project website says the campus reuses about 110 acres within the 750+ acre Dickerson energy campus at 21200 Martinsburg Road. County moratorium actions in 2026 have paused new data center development applications.
notes: Capacity_mw from Server Country tracker; official Montgomery Planning source confirms data center/BESS conditional-use request but did not expose MW in the quick extracted text.

status_detail: Prince George's County Council created a Qualified Data Center Task Force under CR-016-2025 after concern over data center siting; the county task force page links the final report and site-selection inventory. News and tracker sources identify the former Landover Mall site as the controversial approved/proposed data center project. A 2026 executive order and later council actions placed temporary holds/moratoria on data center permit applications while policy is developed.
notes: Capacity not found. County source verifies task-force/moratorium context; Baxtel and local news identify the Landover Mall project and developer.
